articles.title: Recruiting under Canada’s international student cap: Six strategic enrolment gaps that matter
articles.summary: Recruitment teams across Canada are struggling to meet enrolment targets despite the international student cap, as new student arrivals fell by 61% last year—lower than even during the COVID-19 pandemic. The cap is no longer a binding constraint for most institutions, since very few have been using their full allocated quotas, and the primary challenges now lie in demand generation and application approvals.
articles.insight:
Canada’s sharp 61% drop in new international student arrivals—exceeding pandemic-era lows—suggests weakening demand or systemic barriers in key source markets, though it remains unclear whether this reflects broader global sentiment shifts or Canada-specific policy fatigue and visa processing delays.  
Admissions teams should track application volumes, visa refusal rates, and enrolment yield trends across shared source countries—particularly India, Nigeria, and China—to assess whether Canada’s struggles signal emerging competitive opportunities or shared systemic risks requiring proactive market intelligence.

articles.title: US Department of State issued 23% fewer study visas to international students in 2025
articles.summary: The US Department of State issued 23% fewer F-1, M-1, and J-1 student visas to international students in 2025 compared to 2024. Among these, F-1 visa issuances—used by degree-seeking students—declined by one-third during the same period.
articles.insight:
The 23% drop in US student visas—especially the 33% decline in F-1 issuances—may reflect tighter visa adjudication, shifting geopolitical perceptions, or reduced application volumes, though it’s unclear whether this signals weaker underlying demand or procedural constraints.  
Admissions teams should track real-time application and enrolment data by origin country, monitor visa refusal rates and processing times, and assess how peer destinations’ policies and messaging are resonating with prospective students amid evolving global mobility trends.

articles.title: BCA season: UKVI is checking its list, we’re checking ours twice
articles.summary: The article discusses the post-BCA (Border, Citizenship and Immigration) season period when UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) reviews its list of licensed education sponsors while sponsors simultaneously review their own compliance records. Due to delays in data sharing, UKVI’s list and sponsors’ internal records may not align, creating potential discrepancies in sponsor status verification.
articles.insight:
This news signals potential short-term administrative friction for UK-bound international students, as misaligned sponsor lists could delay visa processing or cause confusion—though it doesn’t directly indicate shifts in demand, sentiment, or policy, its timing may amplify existing anxieties in key source markets like India or Nigeria.  
Admissions teams should monitor UKVI’s updated sponsor list and liaise with UK partners to verify status continuity, while preparing clear, proactive communications for applicants about possible verification delays—not as an immediate crisis, but as a prudent operational checkpoint.
